structured_output.hypothesis: If marine forms of life change almost simultaneously worldwide, then the same marine genera will make their first (and last) appearances in the same or adjacent geological stages in widely separated regions, so that regional faunal turnover is synchronous at stage-level resolution.
structured_output.pass_criterion: Take marine genera with at least 5 PBDB occurrences, on at least two of the continental regions (North America, Europe, Asia, Australasia, South America, Africa), with at least 3 occurrences in each region. For each, compute the regional first-appearance stage (from the occurrence age-range fields) in each region. Claim is supported if, across genus-by-region-pair comparisons, at least 75% have first-appearance stages differing by at most 1 stage, and the Spearman correlation of regional first-appearance midpoint ages (Ma) between region pairs is at least 0.9. As a control, within-pair differences must be much smaller than the randomised-genus null: the median absolute difference in Ma must be below 25% of the null median from 1000 permutations.
structured_output.fail_criterion: Claim is refuted if fewer than 50% of genus region-pair comparisons agree within 1 stage, or the Spearman correlation of regional first-appearance ages between region pairs is below 0.7, or the median absolute difference exceeds 50% of the permutation null median. Results between these bounds are inconclusive, not support.
structured_output.interpretation: Darwin's 'forms of life' means genera and species, here taken as marine genera. 'Almost simultaneously, in a broad geological sense' is read as agreement within one geological stage (typically about 2 to 10 Myr) rather than exact contemporaneity. 'Throughout the world' is operationalised as distant continental regions, using present-day coordinates and palaeocoordinates where available. 'Correlated by fossils' is operationalised as consistent first-appearance ordering across regions. Modern caveat: apparent synchrony in PBDB depends partly on stage assignments that were themselves made by fossil correlation, which risks circularity. Using the numeric max_ma and min_ma ages, and the radiometrically calibrated time scale where available, reduces but does not remove this. Sampling bias (Signor-Lipps effect) shifts regional first appearances later than true origination. Only the marine environment is tested, matching the claim's scope.

dataset.name: The Paleobiology Database
dataset.why_it_fits: PBDB holds fossil occurrences with taxon name, geographic coordinates and palaeocoordinates, environment, and numeric age bounds (max_ma, min_ma) plus interval names (early_interval, late_interval). These fields let us compute first appearances of marine genera by region and compare them in time. The site offers a download interface and a public data API for occurrences. The DOI is null because the database as a whole has no single DOI.
